page: Amazon Web Services m8gb.48xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Graviton family built on the arm64 ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture. It features 192 dedicated physical cores operating at 2.7 GHz with a single thread per core, delivering 192 vCPUs alongside 768 GB of total system memory. The core-to-memory ratio is configured at 4 GB per core. The instance provides 400 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth and operates on the Nitro hypervisor. It contains no onboard GPUs and provides no bundled local NVMe storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistence.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional multi-core scalability and memory throughput. The server achieves top-tier results in multi-core stress-ng testing, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and software compilation via Clang. Memory bandwidth reaches 960.61 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 483.46 GB/sec for writes. Similarly, operational benchmarks demonstrate high throughput, with static web serving handling 230.42 GB/sec and Redis executing over 359 million SET operations per second. In contrast, single-core execution across stress-ng and Geekbench falls within the average middle tier, and CPU-based LLM inference performance remains modest.

The hardware profile delivers dense multi-threaded compute efficiency across its 192 physical cores without simultaneous multithreading overhead. Because the instance lacks integrated storage and hardware accelerators, it is engineered primarily for memory-balanced concurrent enterprise applications. Best-fit workloads include distributed in-memory caching, large-scale web serving fleets, parallel code compilation, container orchestration nodes, and distributed database services.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gb.48xlarge is a general-purpose cloud server powered by AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 Graviton processors. It features 192 dedicated physical cores running at 2.7 GHz with single-threading, paired with 768 GB of memory (4 GB per core) and a 400 Gbps network interface. The instance includes no discrete GPUs and features no local instance storage. Benchmark metrics demonstrate top-tier multi-core computing power and memory throughput, scoring exceptionally well in multi-threaded decompression, Clang compilation, database operations, and high-volume Redis operations. Single-thread performance is moderate compared to dedicated high-frequency instances. The server provides strong efficiency for horizontally scalable and highly threaded workloads, making it well suited for large Redis clusters, high-throughput static web serving, container orchestration pools, parallel compilation pipelines, and memory-balanced enterprise database systems requiring heavy network and multi-core throughput.
